clue.text: Magic transport needs fourth of combustion chambers to run like clockwork

indicators.note: fourth of tells you to count along the next word and keep only its fourth letter

blocks.note: c-o-m-b: the fourth letter
chambers are rooms
a clock ticks as it runs

explanation.surface: A wizard's vehicle needs an engine part to keep running smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches in folklore fly about on a besom, the household sweeping brush serving as their means of travel.

clue.text: Born high or low, pondered changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides asks you to swap right for left, the abbreviations for the two sides, within the word for pondered

blocks.note: feeling low is feeling blue
brooded means pondered gloomily

explanation.surface: Whether high-born or lowly, someone thought about switching allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: In BROODED the R (right) changes to L (left), giving BLOODED.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats were said to have blue blood, so someone of noble birth is described this way.

clue.text: Surprisingly content to ignore every new music group

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly has not gone in the expected order, so the letters are rearranged
to ignore every one means each occurrence of the following letter is dropped, not just one

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A band unexpectedly happy to skip all the latest material.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTENT loses both its Ns, and the remaining five letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians, or a piece written for them, is the standard term in chamber music.

clue.text: Promotion of publicly funded entertainment starting three months early?

indicators.note: the word's opening month abbreviation is swapped for the month that falls three months before it

blocks.note: a junket is a jolly paid for out of public money

explanation.surface: Advertising a taxpayer-funded show that opens a quarter earlier than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: JUNKETING starts with JUN (June); three months earlier is MAR (March), so JUN becomes MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling and advertising products is the business of the commercial department devoted to publicity.

clue.text: Revolutionary to run broadcasting company

blocks.note: to trot is to run slowly
Sky is the British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A rebel off to manage a TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a leader of the Russian Revolution of 1917 and founder of the Red Army.

clue.text: Hybrid animal has feline claw shortened

indicators.note: shortened says the preceding word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a feline is a cat
a talon is a claw

explanation.surface: A crossbred creature whose cat-like claw has been clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: TALON loses its last letter to leave TALO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattalo is a cross between domestic cattle and the American bison, bred in North America.

clue.text: Soundlessly defying comprehension?

blocks.note: surface reading: silently, without making a noise
setter's reading: in a way that cannot be sounded, as a sea too deep to measure with a plumb line

explanation.surface: Something silently baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: To sound water is to measure its depth; water whose bottom cannot be reached is literally beyond measure in fathoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impossible to understand is figuratively too deep to plumb, a sense taken from measuring the sea.

clue.text: Ordering of pieces from mint is a must for me

definitions.text: Ordering of pieces from mint is a must for me

indicators.note: ordering means putting things into a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the four words taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin collector insists on ordering freshly struck coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: someone for whom getting pieces from the mint is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin collector, for whom ordering newly struck coins from the mint is essential, is the subject of this sentence.

clue.text: Madcap display with tops off carelessly

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of each word is its first letter, and both lose it

blocks.note: zany means madcap
a show is a display

explanation.surface: A crazy exhibition put on topless and without care.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something any old way is doing it without care or in a haphazard manner.

clue.text: Was a loudmouth Liberal before getting into power?

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so the first pieces are placed within the word for power

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
ere is an old word for before
to have a hold over someone is to have power over them

explanation.surface: Was the Liberal a bigmouth before taking office?
explanation.definitionFit: To holler is to yell or shout loudly, as a noisy loudmouth does.

clue.text: Jesus follower uplifted youth with spirited stuff, just past two o'clock?

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means read from bottom to top, so these words run backwards

blocks.note: a lad is a youth
gamy can mean plucky or spirited
to ram is to stuff or cram
on a clock face used as a compass, east-north-east lies just after two

explanation.surface: An elated young disciple with high spirits, a little after two in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Treat the clock as a compass: north at twelve, east at three, so east-north-east sits just past two.
explanation.definitionFit: She was one of the women who travelled with Jesus and the first witness to the resurrection in the Gospels.

clue.text: Snake swallowing piece representing half or quarter of artists

indicators.note: a snake swallowing something holds it inside, so the next piece goes within

blocks.note: a boa is a large snake
hemi- is the word element meaning half, as in hemisphere

explanation.surface: A snake gulping down a piece of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemia came to mean any district where artists and writers live unconventionally.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian area is one where artists live, the term borrowed from the Czech region via French usage for Romani.

clue.text: Hater of Brussels sprouts to start with mushroom, having obsessed about removing cap

indicators.note: to start with means only the opening letter of the preceding word is used
a cap sits on top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter, which goes
about means going round, so the trimmed word wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: first letter of sprouts
a cep is a porcini mushroom
neurotic means obsessive or anxious

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes Brussels sprouts, starting with mushroom and obsessing over it.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels and sprouts look like a pair, but Brussels is the seat of the European Union and belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to increasing the powers of the European Union, based in Brussels, is described by this term.

clue.text: Suave person who won't keep your interest without rifling through it

blocks.note: smooth means suave

blocks.clueFragment: person who won't keep your interest
blocks.note: a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A slick but dull person who leaves you cold without going through your things.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifling is the spiral grooving cut inside a gun barrel; a gun lacking it has an ungrooved barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun whose barrel is not grooved inside, like a musket or shotgun, has no rifling through it.

clue.text: Perhaps excel at making statements extreme

blocks.note: to utter is to say or make a statement
to excel at something is, loosely, to do it most

explanation.surface: Maybe someone shines at making bold claims.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, excelling at speaking is doing it most, so the two parts sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttermost is an older form meaning furthest or greatest in degree, the same as utmost.

clue.text: Prudish damage to comment, deleting articles

indicators.note: the indefinite article a is struck out of each of the two words

blocks.note: to maim is to damage
to say is to comment

explanation.surface: A prim objection to harm done to a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimsy, from Lewis Carroll, has come to mean primly affected, prissy or over-delicate in manner.

clue.text: Hunting breed incapable of steady gait?

blocks.note: first meaning: a crossbred dog used for poaching and coursing
second meaning: one who staggers or sways

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: one who lurches cannot walk steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog, usually greyhound crossed with collie, shares its name with someone who staggers about.

clue.text: Repeatedly hit old salts in refuge?

blocks.note: to batter is to strike again and again
sea dogs are veteran sailors
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Beating up old sailors who are sheltering somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs Home is a famous London animal rescue centre; 'in' looks like a link word but gives the last part.
explanation.definitionFit: The London charity has rehomed stray dogs since Victorian times, making it a shelter for animals.

clue.text: Not speaking, I forgot to mention complaint

blocks.note: keeping mum is staying silent
a postscript adds what the writer forgot

explanation.surface: Silent, and then remembering one more thing to grumble about.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an illness, and this viral infection swells the salivary glands.

clue.text: Work against a municipal lack of transparency

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written
city used as an adjective, as in city council

explanation.surface: Opposing a council's secretive way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the quality of being opaque, that is not letting light through, or figuratively being obscure.

clue.text: Section of Norman arch is thrown into disorder?

indicators.note: a section of the following words is a run of letters cut from inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word through the start of the last

explanation.surface: Part of a Norman archway is knocked down in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' serves twice: its first letter ends the hidden run, while the definition reads 'into disorder', a person who is keen on chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes government and order is a person keen on, or into, lawlessness and chaos.

clue.text: Hen scrabbling in grass, ready for mates?

indicators.note: a scrabbling hen scratches about, scattering things, so the letters are jumbled
in puts the jumbled letters inside the word for grass

blocks.note: taken as written
the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A hen scratching about in the grass, looking for a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A female animal on heat is in season and receptive to mating.

clue.text: Some heated argle-bargle over site of capital

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of them is used
over means turned over, read from right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word through the start of the hyphenated one

explanation.surface: A rather heated row about where the capital should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia, and formerly of Yugoslavia, so it is where a capital stands.

clue.text: 9 in the morning, stopping long speech

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so it sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a screed is a long piece of writing or speech
am is ante meridiem, morning

explanation.surface: Nine o'clock, and a long harangue is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 points to the answer at 9-down, HOLLERED, as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollered and this word both mean shouted at the top of one's voice, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Unwelcome blow for man that may be crowned

blocks.note: first meaning: a cold current of air indoors
second meaning: a piece in the board game that becomes a king when it reaches the far side

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a chilly gust through a room and a counter in the British name for checkers.

clue.text: A tiny toll from rise of large deer parasite in egg form

clue.text: Region that has nothing against blocking a royal

blocks.note: O looks like zero
v is short for versus
a prince is a royal

clue.text: Publicity favoured pushy salesman's data, on paper

blocks.note: PR is public relations
in means fashionable, favoured
a tout pesters people to buy

clue.text: Water regulator favoured to provide motor part

blocks.note: a tap controls the flow of water

clue.text: Promise to fix toilet pan

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Disagreement on acceptance of a queen's duty

taken as written

clue.text: Opinionated medic giving nothing away during broadcast with European

indicators.note: giving away a zero means the round letter shaped like nought is dropped from the word

in means during, as in 'in the night'

clue.text: Working at it, cheer up, to improve one's health

clue.text: Charmer, bachelor in art school, that might be handy in a street fight

definitions.text: that might be handy in a street fight

blocks.note: a witch casts charms

explanation.surface: A charming single man at art college who knows how to look after himself in a brawl.

clue.text: Manipulation of planimeter's unaffected by fourth dimension?

clue.text: Like a ruddy camp fire?

blocks.note: surface padding that frames the clue as a description
first meaning: a mild British oath, a polite stand-in for bloody, and also glowing red
second meaning: flamboyantly and theatrically effeminate, in slang
surface padding, though a fire is literally ablaze, which backs up the reading

clue.text: Financial juggling, random, with good earnings primarily for the bottom line?

first letters of good and earnings

clue.text: Press become tedious, with old content

clue.text: Good book with a final twist, its first section being trumpery

taken as written

clue.text: Mock coach admitting own goal

taken as written

clue.text: Not fully getting to grips with things, very short of staff?
